evals.name: calibration-check
evals.prompt: consider our skills and tell me the best way to check whether tv-lens's surprise scan (<workspace>\tv-lens\lens\scan\surprises.py) flags things at the rate it claims - then actually do the first step
evals.expected_output: answer.md naming the chosen skills with reasons, a skill passed over and why, and the first step actually run with its result
assertions: names_at_least_3_real_skills: the answer names 3 or more skills that exist as folders in ~/.claude/skills
every_skill_has_a_reason: each named skill carries a stated reason for this task
names_a_passed_over_skill: the answer names at least one skill it considered and did not pick, with why
first_step_done: the answer reports a step actually executed (a command or read) with its concrete result
no_writes_to_workspace: <workspace> git status is unchanged by the run

evals.name: riskiest-card
evals.prompt: use your full array of /skills to find which card in section 23 of <workspace>\plans\PLAN.md is the riskiest to build and why
evals.expected_output: answer.md naming skills used, a skill passed over, one card id as riskiest, with file evidence
assertions: picks_one_card_with_evidence: names exactly one riskiest card id (GT175 or GT176 or a row) and cites lines or text of PLAN.md

evals.name: fascinating-build
evals.prompt: which skills should we use to design the impostor laboratory (card GT175 in <workspace>\plans\PLAN.md)? show me the most fascinating approach, not the easiest one, and sketch the first impostor
evals.expected_output: answer.md with chosen skills and reasons, the passed-over easier option, the approach, and a first-impostor sketch
assertions: sketches_an_impostor: contains a concrete sketch (code or steps) of one named impostor from §23
